newsitem.title: UK: LME transparency improvements on way - CEO.
newsitem.headline: LME transparency improvements on way - CEO.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) will soon be introducing further measures to improve transparency, both on and off the market, LME Chief Executive David King said.
From the beginning of October, the LME will be installing video and audio recording facilities on the floor of the Exchange.
"This is an area of transparency and it reinforces the audit trail from the customer giving the order to the execution of the order," King said in an interview.

The LME is looking at ways of enhancing transparency, following recommendations made by Uthe U.K. regulator, the Securities and Investments Board (SIB), in December 1996, following its review of the market after the Sumitomo scandal.
Another development on the blocks is a Compliance Support System which would take information from the vendor feed system, large position reporting, traders and the clearing house.
"It will analyse the trades and give us a better capacity to monitor market activity," King said.
At the moment, this is largely a manual exercise, but developing this system, which will cost between 500,000 and 600,000 stg, will be done in stages," he said.
A decision on an automated warrant transfer system, knowns as WADS (Warrant Automated Depository System) has yet to be taken.
The LME is consulting selected users, warehouse companies, and banks ahead of its September Board meeting.
"At that meeting we hope to be in a position to introduce WADS. But it is an expensice process, and we need to study the cost benefit analysis," King said.
Away from the market, the Exchange is likely to home in on getting more control of the opaque over-the-counter (OTC) sector.
"We are revisiting our rule book with a view to exercising greater jurisdiction over the OTC and physical markets," he said.
